**Exclude subsecond fields from wall-clock conversion.** For timezone-aware nanosecond timestamps near the limit, `_local_wall_clock` can overflow and produce incorrect subsecond results. For representable conversions, the whole-second offset leaves those results unchanged. Excluding these fields also avoids transition-table and full-column work.
Suggested fix

```diff --- "a/python/cudf_polars/cudf_polars/dsl/expressions/datetime.py" +++ "b/python/cudf_polars/cudf_polars/dsl/expressions/datetime.py" @@ -1106,7 +1106,10 @@ # reads them from the local wall clock, not from the UTC instant. _LOCAL_FIELDS: ClassVar[frozenset[Name]] = frozenset( { - *_COMPONENT_MAP.keys(), + *( + _COMPONENT_MAP.keys() + - {Name.Millisecond, Name.Microsecond, Name.Nanosecond} + ), Name.Date, Name.DaysInMonth, Name.IsLeapYear, ```
Committable suggestion

> **IMPORTANT** > Review the replacement and indentation, then test before committing. ```suggestion *( _COMPONENT_MAP.keys() - {Name.Millisecond, Name.Microsecond, Name.Nanosecond} ), ```

Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title names the main change: cudf-polars now reads local wall-clock time for calendar fields on timezone-aware datetime columns. It matches the raw summary, the description, and the linked issue scope. It is a conventional-commit title and is specific enough for a reviewer scanning history.
Full details: Description check

**Explanation** The description explains the bug (calendar fields computed from the stored UTC instant instead of the column's local wall clock), the fix (converting to local wall-clock time before field extraction in TemporalFunction), the affected fields, the new test, and the scope exclusion for dt.to_string(). This matches the changeset, so the check passes.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check

**Explanation** All changes support the calendar-field fix. The `_LOCAL_FIELDS` set and the constructor condition extend the existing time zone setup. The evaluate-time pre-conversion reuses `_local_wall_clock`, as the PR states. The ToString branch change only merges that name into the existing condition, and ToString is not in `_LOCAL_FIELDS`, so its evaluation behavior is unchanged. The added test covers the affected fields. No unrelated edits appear in the reviewed diff for datetime.py. I did not inspect the test file diff directly; its scope is taken from the summary.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** [`#25117`] Calendar-field requirement: met by the diff. In datetime.py, `_LOCAL_FIELDS` lists `_COMPONENT_MAP` keys plus Date, DaysInMonth, IsLeapYear, IsoYear, OrdinalDay, Quarter, Week, Century and Millennium. In `evaluate`, a field op with a time zone descriptor passes its input through `_local_wall_clock` before extraction. This addresses the reported `dt.hour()` UTC-read bug and the related fields in the issue. The reviewed head includes test_datetime_fields_read_local_wall_clock, which covers these fields on Asia/Kathmandu and America/New_York near midnight, year end and DST change. The PR author reports 20 failures on main and a pass with this change. I did not re-run tests. [`#25117`] `dt.to_string()` requirement: the issue requests GPU output that matches CPU output for `to_string` (`+0000` instead of `+0545`). The PR description and PR objectives state this part is excluded and tracked in `#23935`. The constructor branch for ToString already sets time zone descriptors at the merge base. I did not verify the ToString evaluation path at the reviewed head, so I cannot establish whether the issue's to_string requirement is met. **Resolution** Confirm, with the issue reproducer or an equivalent test, that `dt.to_string("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M%z")` on a UTC-to-Asia/Kathmandu column returns `2020-01-01T05:45+0545` on the GPU engine at the reviewed head. If that output is not produced, the to_string part of `#25117` remains unmet in this PR. Either this PR must cover it, or the scope split to `#23935` must be confirmed by the maintainers.
